relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with genetically confirmed SSADH deficiency: "a homozygous pathogenic mutation in the ALDH5A1 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). No ALDH5A1 variant description is printed, so the variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'; zygosity 'homozygous' and pathogenicity 'pathogenic' come from the sentence about this patient. Vital status 'alive' rests on same-day discharge after the procedure. Onset 'during the infancy after birth' is when hypotonia and developmental delay were followed up. 'Cognitively delayed' was mapped to the checklist item intellectual disability (judgement). Anxiety and agitation were excluded from 'the absence of anxiety or agitation', a preoperative statement about this patient. Normal preoperative laboratory tests were recorded as excluded abnormalities of each named test (D-27). Intra- and postoperative absences (seizures, rigidity, autonomic instability, delayed awakening, respiratory distress) were recorded as excluded with timing in severity_or_detail. MRI white matter/subcortical T2 hyperintensities do not name the globus pallidus, subthalamic or dentate nuclei, so that checklist item is not reported. 'Limited cooperation' (reason for anesthesia) versus 'he was cooperative' on examination: not recorded as features; noted here. No contradictions on phenotypic features. First author: the header prints 'Savaş Zülfü'; recorded 'Zülfü' as surname assuming given-name-first order (uncertain).

treatment_summary.value: multiple dental extractions and restorations under general anesthesia (midazolam, lidocaine, propofol, fentanyl, rocuronium; sevoflurane maintenance; ondansetron; local lidocaine with epinephrine; paracetamol; sugammadex reversal); no history of anticonvulsant drug use
span: scheduled for multiple extractions and restorations under general anesthesia

Firstly, low‐dose midazolam (0.05 mg/kg) was administered. Then, lidocaine (1 mg/kg), propofol (3 mg/kg), fentanyl (1 mcg/kg), and rocuronium (0.75 mg/kg) were used to facilitate endotracheal intubation.
Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane in a 50% air/oxygen mixture.
paracetamol (10 mg/kg) was administered for postoperative pain prophylaxis, and sugammadex (4 mg/kg) was administered
he had no history of seizures and no history of anticonvulsant drug use
